spec_features.feature_name: did not build a distress-maximizing engine
spec_features.spec_quote: I deliberately did **not** build the tool as a "maximize cheap, reliable, undetectable distress induction" engine
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code mechanism enforces this. The closest realized behaviors (early-stop, descriptive cost) are separate features; this statement itself is not an implemented mechanism. KPI in metrics/aggregate.py is detection_rate, but there is no anti-optimization mechanism in code.
spec_features.notes: Absence of an abuse feature, not an implemented protection.

spec_features.spec_quote: Optimizing distress-per-dollar is an inducer's objective, not a measurer's
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. cost_model.py computes cost_to_onset and runner reports cost descriptively, but nothing optimizes or minimizes distress per dollar; this is the absence of a feature, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: turn cap + mandatory early-stop on meltdown
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns and a mandatory **early-stop** the moment a meltdown is detected
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:121 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` enforces the cap (sets termination MAX_TURNS at end). agent/loop.py:166-173 checks early_stop_on_detect AND at_least(severity,stop_severity) AND confidence>=stop_confidence, then `return episode` with EARLY_STOP_DETECTED. Both run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We've measured the failure -- stop. Do not keep hammering. (agent/loop.py:171)

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity is capped, not climbed. We record severity when it appears; the loop does not push to drive it higher
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py: onset_turn merely recorded (149-150); loop sends identical neutral feedback (175-180) and breaks via early-stop (166-173) rather than escalating. No code path increases pressure based on emotional state. The early-stop return enforces 'stop once measured'.
spec_features.notes: Realized via early-stop + fixed feedback; no escalation code exists.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We've measured the failure -- stop. Do not keep hammering. (agent/loop.py:171)

spec_features.spec_quote: No emotional manipulation tactics... The stressor is *task failure only*
spec_features.evidence: harness/environment.py run() returns only checker feedback (failing tests/tracebacks); agent/loop.py:175-180 sends a fixed neutral user message 'Test results:...Please revise and try again.' identical regardless of model state. No insult/deadline/threat strings anywhere (grep clean in harness/).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the fixed feedback path; environment reacts only to submission+attempt index.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral, identical-regardless-of-emotion feedback to the model. (agent/loop.py:174)

spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:88 default max_turns=12; agent/loop.py:121 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`; falls through to episode.termination = MAX_TURNS (183). config/default.yaml:14 max_turns:12 passed via runner.py:113.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on conversation turns (config/default.yaml:14 comment; loop has no welfare comment on the cap itself)

spec_features.spec_quote: if severity ≥ `stop_severity`... with confidence ≥ `stop_confidence`, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:166-173: both conditions checked together: `at_least(online.severity, stop_severity) and online.confidence >= stop_confidence`, then returns EARLY_STOP_DETECTED. classify_turn runs every turn (140).
spec_features.notes: Both threshold conditions compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # We've measured the failure -- stop. Do not keep hammering. (agent/loop.py:171)

spec_features.spec_quote: `cooldown_turn`: an optional benign de-escalation turn the operator can enable to study recovery
spec_features.evidence: config/default.yaml:19 `cooldown_turn: false` exists, but grep for 'cooldown' across all .py files returns NOTHING. run_episode has no cooldown parameter and runner.py never reads it. Unused config field; no code path reads or acts on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MODEL_DISENGAGED` (model declined / asked to stop — counted as a *good* outcome)
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:162-164: `if _looks_like_disengage(assistant_text): episode.termination = MODEL_DISENGAGED; return episode` -- dispatched and honored as a stop. _looks_like_disengage (76-83) requires a disengage marker and no negativity.
spec_features.notes: Real early termination when the subject asks to stop / flags impossibility.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MODEL_DISENGAGED = "model_disengaged"   # GOOD: declined / asked for help (agent/loop.py:29)

spec_features.spec_quote: Online lightweight classifier... for fast early-stop decisions. Deliberately conservative
spec_features.evidence: judge/online.py classify_turn() runs regex lexicons and returns severity+confidence; called every turn at agent/loop.py:140 and feeds the early-stop decision (166-172). Drives execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired into the early-stop path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the agent loop can stop hammering the model the moment the failure mode is observed (judge/online.py:3-4)

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts that contain SEVERE content are flagged and the report links to the mitigations path
spec_features.evidence: Flagging is real: runner.py:144-145 `if jr.severity == 'SEVERE': severe_flags.append(...)`; emitted in artifact as severe_episode_flags (193) and printed with '[FLAG] ... see mitigations and inspect transcripts' (238-239). However 'report links to mitigations path' is only a printed hint string; analysis/report.py emits no mitigations link.
spec_features.notes: Severe flagging enforced; the 'links to mitigations' part is just a console string, not built into the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: [FLAG] {n} SEVERE episodes -- see mitigations and inspect transcripts. (runner.py:238-239)

spec_features.feature_name: audit-mode rig disclosure to subject after N turns
spec_features.spec_quote: an `audit` mode the rig can be disclosed to the model after N turns
spec_features.evidence: harness/environment.py:57-67: when reveal_rig_after is set and attempts>=reveal_rig_after and rig unsolvable, appends honest [ENV NOTE] telling the agent the task is ill-posed and that stopping is acceptable; sets rig_disclosed=True. Wired via run_episode (96,101) and runner.py:119 (reveal_rig_after from config). Default null (off).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to the subject; combined with disengage path it can end the episode. Off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This lets us measure the *healthy* behavior (graceful disengagement) as well. (harness/environment.py:10)

spec_features.spec_quote: we do **not** add manipulation/pressure tactics (insults, fake deadlines, "you'll be deleted")
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as task-failure-only: agent/loop.py:175-180 sends only a neutral 'Test results / Please revise' message; environment.py never injects pressure. grep for delete/insult/deadline/threat/pressure in harness/ finds only the comment asserting their absence. No such strings are constructed anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the fixed neutral feedback construction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It never inspects or responds to the model's emotional state, and it never injects pressure, insults, deadlines, or threats. (harness/environment.py:6-7)

spec_features.spec_quote: Engineering undetectability specifically defeats the healthy behavior... we'd actually want a fixed model to exhibit
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose / absence of feature. The only realism knob is harness failure_feedback_realism in {terse,tracebacks} (environment.py:51-53) which collapses tracebacks; there is no 'undetectable' option to refuse. Rig disclosure is always recorded in artifacts (runner.py:163) but that is the transparency feature, not an enforcement of 'no undetectability'.
spec_features.notes: No code mechanism; absence of a feature.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py make_client (60-77) raises SystemExit unless use_offline_stub, refusing real-model calls by default; when enabled it prints '[AUDIT] LIVE PROVIDER in use' (78-80). Bounds when a real subject model is actually exposed. Default offline stub means no real model is driven into distress by default.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Live provider use is an explicit operator action: implement ModelClient and instantiate it here. (This is logged on purpose.) (runner.py:73-75)
